objects: For every nonnegative initial offset c, natural finite horizon T, real increment stream b with b_t>=0 for t<T, and real function f continuous, nonincreasing and nonnegative on [0,infinity), define s_0=c and s_(t+1)=s_t+b_t. Then sum(t<T)b_t*f(s_(t+1)) is at most the integral of f from c to s_T. All zero cases are included.
delta: Lean b_t is source a_(t+1), while c is the separate source a0. The ambient real extension is constrained only on the nonnegative half-line, including relative continuity at zero; negative arguments are unused. The public type retains source f>=0 although this proof does not use that premise. No positivity, global regularity or integrability premise is added.
proof: Nonnegative increments order all cumulative endpoints inside the nonnegative half-line. Restrict the given continuity to each compact increment interval to obtain integrability. Antitonicity bounds the constant right-endpoint value by f(x) on that interval. Its integral is the actual increment times the right-endpoint value. Sum these comparisons and telescope the adjacent integrals; repeated endpoints and the empty horizon require no division or special positivity assumption.
